summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of tin oxide on silicon using tin(II)acetylacetonate as a novel precursor and ozone as an oxidizer. The ALD process was carried out within a temperature range of 175–300 °C, resulting in a growth rate of 0.1 ± 0.01 nm/cycle. The films exhibited a clean SnOx–Si interface without the formation of SiO2 or other interfacial reaction products, making them suitable for transparent conducting oxide (TCO) applications.
evidence: The film growth rate was found to be 0.1 6 0.01 nm/cycle within the wide ALD temperature window of 175–300 /C14 C using ozone; no film growth was observed with water or oxygen. X-ray photoelectron spectra showed the formation of a clean SnOx–Si interface. The resistivity of the SnOx films was calculated to be 0.3 X cm. Results of this work demonstrate the possibility of introducing Sn(acac) 2 as tin precursor to deposit conducting ALD SnOx thin films on a silicon surface, with clean interface and no formation of undesired SiO2 or other interfacial reaction products, for transparent conducting oxide applications.
